verdict: MIXED MIND FAILS AS A STEERER; WHOLE-ANSWER POOL HAS REAL HEADROOM BUT THE GENIUS AGREEMENT SCORE CANNOT HARVEST IT - P FAILS THE FROZEN BAND. (1) Mixing genius weights into the model's own output weights is a NO-OP on greedy decode: calibration tied 4/12 across alpha 0/0.5/1.0 (identical correct-sets), and the disclosed probe shows trajectories identical at alpha up to 8.0. The genius head was compiled FROM the model's own behavior and agrees with its argmax ~96% of the time - it is a compressed mirror, not an independent expert, so 'both minds holding context together' adds nothing the model does not already think. M arm skipped per frozen rule. (2) Whole-answer parallelism itself is validated: 4/4 unique drafts on every item, and the best-of-4 oracle ceiling is 18/30 = 60.0% vs single-answer 50.0% - the pool DOES contain better answers, the user's intuition is right. (3) But the genius refinement step cannot find them: raw agreement saturates (top-score ties on 12/30 items), recovered 0/3 salvageable items, and its shorter-tie-break threw away 3 correct anchors (tie-break picked a wrong, shorter sampled draft). Winner strict 12/30 = 40.0% vs anchor 50.0% = -10.0pp -> FAIL per frozen band (and 3.49x wall cost). HONEST BOTTOM LINE: per the user's own rule, P as implemented is NOT a win - accuracy dropped and wall time grew 3.5x. The experiment localizes the failure precisely: the pool has the answers (oracle 60%), the selector is the wall (agreement saturates at 1.0). The fix is a discriminating score - e.g. genius-model disagreement density or confidence-profile matching - not more drafts.
